**Nearest / distinct payoff:** model-based-planning chooses from a model; this changes an obstacle during execution and charges observation/replanning overhead.

**Computed primary model:** Unit-cost undirected graph edgesA–B,B–G,A–C,C–D,D–G. Original shortest planA→B→G. Obstacle closesB–G immediately after firstmoveA→B. Fixed plan attempts blockedB→G and fails after2attempted moves. Reactive executor senses before each move (cost.5), recomputes BFS and atB goesB→A→C→D→G:5moves total,5observations, total cost7.5 and goal reached.

**Countercase / boundary:** No obstacle change: fixed plan reachesG in2moves cost2; reactive path also2moves but2observations add1, cost3. Reactivity can rescue this changed-world case while costing overhead in the stable case; no universal agent advantage or free knowledge of a future closure is admitted.

**Prediction / transfer recall:** Predict the reactive next move once atB and closure is observed; recall stable conditions can make the original fixed plan cheaper.

**Intervention / retained witness:** Execute step advances the actual position and closure time; Fixed/Reactive share the same environment event. Stable world recomputes costs. Retain original blocked fixed trace and reactive route alongside stable cost contrast; never teleport pastB.
